correctness.rationale: For generic points of an affine-regular pentagon, affine diameters are exactly the five edge--opposite-vertex sweep families, so multiplicity is the overlap count of five explicit triangles. Each internal pentagram diagonal is a side of two such triangles, making the generic multiplicity parity invariant under crossings; a boundary-near cell has count one. The fivefold cell is the central pentagram pentagon. Exact Q(sqrt(5)) area calculations give its normalized area, and the other two level areas follow from normalization and the exact integral of the five triangle indicators. The packaged checker verifies all algebraic identities and incidence certificates.

value.rationale: Pointwise affine-diameter multiplicity is a classical structural object, while the 2014 source introduced its mean as a quantitative invariant. The triangle is characterized by constant multiplicity three, so the affine-regular pentagon is the first canonical odd polygon where a nonconstant distribution is mathematically natural. The finding completely resolves that distribution, including the fivefold core and variance, rather than computing an arbitrary isolated value.
